title: Bootswarm Shift Handoff & Troubleshoot Notebook — Week Mar 9–15 2026
content:
Purpose
This is the bootswarm shift log for the private-deploy field team covering Mar 9–15, 2026. The doc is a hybrid handoff + troubleshooting notebook to capture work done across multiple installs (VPC and on-prem), outstanding customer blockers, and suggested runbook edits. Use this when taking the next shift; most recent notes at top.

Summary highlights (top-line)
- Zenith Health: intermittent large-request stalls traced to MTU mismatch on leaf switch -> slow path for large KV cache warmups. Partial mitigation applied (jumbo mtu 9000 -> 1500) pending network change window.
- Kappa Commerce: NFS client flapping causing model cache corruption on nodes with >256GB RAM. Worked around with read-only mount + rsync rehydrate.
- Private install telemetry gap: missing node-level kernel livepatch logs in install artifact bundle; added one-line shim to installer to collect /var/log/kern.log and dmesg output.
- Two follow-ups for engineering: (1) kernel log collection PR, (2) deterministic restart ordering for redis-kv cache after power-fail.

Daily entries
2026-03-15 (shift lead: Aisha)
- Handoff from Marcus: Zenith config drift caught after the second large inference job failed (time > 120s). Marcus ran tcpdump and forwarded pcap to neteng.
- Investigation: captured path MTU discovery failing (ICMP-blocking on firewall between cluster and model-store). Observed PMTU discovery packets not making it.
- Action taken: temporary change to endpoint MTU on all model-serving nodes from 9000 to 1500 and restarted net agent. Immediate tail-latency improved from p95 200ms -> 90ms for long requests but some customers still see issues for >64KB payloads.
- Customer comms: Lina opened a support ticket (PLAT-2045) and scheduled a network change window with Zenith for 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC to fix firewall ICMP rule.
- Notes for follow-up: reconcile kernel offload settings (GRO/GSO) after MTU change. Add to runbook: how to rollback MTU safely.

2026-03-14 (shift: Marcus)
- Kappa Commerce install: observed model-serving pod OOMs followed by NFS mount flapping.
- Root cause hypothesis: NFS client on kernel 5.15.0 has a known regresssion under heavy mmap() with high RAM, see INSTALL-512.
- Workaround applied: remounted NFS read-only, rsynced model shards to local ext4 partition, restarted model-serving with local cache path. Service back up; regen cost ~3h for large model.
- Next steps: coordinate with Kappa to evaluate persistent local cache sizing and consider using AWS EBS volume with io1 for throughput.

2026-03-13 (shift: Omar)
- Install-day: on-prem customer 'Orchid Analytics' had brief network split causing corosync elect flapping in our HA overlay.
- Mitigation: forced quorum on primary and drained standby node; manual KV reconciliation required. Documented exact sequence of etcd reconcile commands used (see linked artifact PR).
- Observation: our bootstrap script didn’t detect dual NICs correctly; added a small probe to choose mgmt NIC by gateway route. Patch in review (github PR 321).

Operational runbook suggestions (short term)
- Add step to install artifact collection: include /var/log/kern.log, output of dmesg -T, and `ethtool -k <iface>` for first-hop NICs. Rationale: network offload state was critical to reproducing Zenith issue.
- Add MTU rollback snippet: sequence to change MTU back to 9000 after firewall change window, verify with iperf3 and curl test payloads of 128KB, 512KB.
- NFS resilience: document safe rsync pattern to rehydrate model shards with checksum verification and minimal service downtime.
- Deterministic restart ordering: propose restart order: storage -> model-store -> model-runtime -> sidecars -> tracing. Add check for in-flight KV cache flush.

Open blockers and owners
- PLAT-2045 (Zenith MTU/firewall rule) — owner: Lina Gomez — blocker: customer firewall team not confirming ICMP rule until change window (scheduled).
- INSTALL-512 (NFS kernel regression) — owner: Marcus Chen — blocker: upstream kernel backport schedule; short-term patch to remount with noac currently in customer-run.
- Telemetry collection gap (missing kernel logs) — owner: Omar Wilson — blocker: needs quick PR to installer (low risk).
- Redis-kv restart ordering race on power-fail — owner: Aisha Patel — blocker: needs a small state machine change in runtime to guard restart sequence; roadmap item Q2.

Notes to the next shift
- If you see long-tail stalls >100ms again, immediately check MTU + ICMP (ping -M do -s 1400 <store>) and tcpdump for PMTU discovery (look for DF bit set packets and ICMP unreachable).
- For suspected NFS flaps: check dmesg for 'NFS: server' messages, run `mount -o remount,ro <path>`, and initiate rsync -> systemctl restart redwood-model.service.
- Preserve /var/log/redwood/install.log and upload to PLAT-2045. We need a full bundle for root cause.

Customer snippets (copyable)
- Zenith draft comms: "We've identified a network path MTU issue that intermittently affects large inference requests. We’ve applied a temporary MTU change on our side and scheduled a coordinated firewall change to allow ICMP for PMTU discovery on 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC. During the maintenance window we expect a brief restart of service (~2 minutes)."
- Kappa draft comms: "We observed intermittent NFS client instability that caused temporary model cache corruption. We migrated the model cache to a local disk and restored service. We recommend sizing a persistent local volume to avoid refetch delays; our engineering team will provide sizing recommendations after access to IO metrics."

Telemetry and follow-ups (engineering requests)
- Telemetry: add fields to the install artifact schema: kernel_version, dmesg_snapshot, ethtool_offload_flags, nfs_version. Shorty-term PR to capture those.
- Tests: add a nightly synthetic test that sends 128KB, 256KB, 512KB payloads to a staging model endpoint to exercise PMTU and large-payload path. Compare p95/p99 against baseline.

Meeting notes (sync with NetEng and Customer Success)
- 2026-03-16 sync planned with NetEng at 15:00 PST to walk through Zenith packet captures. Attendees: Lina, Marcus, NetEng: Priya Rao. Goal: confirm ICMP rule change and post-change verification steps.
- 2026-03-17 CS check-in with Kappa to agree on local-volume sizing and escalation plan if kernel patch not backported.

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: rolling MTU change can affect other co-located services if not carefully scoped. Mitigation: perform change in maintenance window with canary nodes and run distributed curl/iperf checks first.
- Risk: ad-hoc local cache migration increases operational cost and engineering support time. Mitigation: provide automated rsync helper in installer and documented rollback.

Loose ideas / wishlist (for product/infra roadmap)
- Installer: optional built-in local-cache mode that transparently keeps a soft-copy of most-used shards on local SSD with TTL/consistency guarantees.
- Runtime: graceful KV cache warmup that can stream missing shards rather than blocking requests; fall back to smaller-token responses with an explanatory header.

Appendix: useful commands / quick-debug snippets
- Check PMTU discovery: `ping -M do -s 1400 <model-store-ip>`
- Capture PMTU fail: `sudo tcpdump -nn -i eth0 host <store-ip> and icmp`
- Collect kernel logs: `sudo journalctl -k -b --no-pager > /tmp/kern.log; dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg.log`
- Safe NFS read-only remount: `sudo mount -o remount,ro /mnt/model-store && rsync -az --progress /mnt/model-store /var/local/model-cache/`
- Restart order snippet: `systemctl stop redwood-tracing; systemctl stop redwood-sidecar; systemctl stop redwood-runtime; systemctl stop redwood-model; systemctl start redwood-model; systemctl start redwood-runtime;`

End-of-week retrospective notes
- What worked: quick isolation of PMTU vs application-layer latency; improved signal from tcpdump + ethtool.
- What didn't: missing kernel-level telemetry made root cause slower to validate.
- Actionables for sprint planning: include the two small PRs (installer telemetry + restart ordering guard) in next sprint; mark deterministic KV restart as medium effort.

If you take the next shift, add your notes here (append-only) and tag relevant JIRA tickets.

-- Aisha (on behalf of bootswarm shift)
